brief.user: Documentation maintainers reviewing repository-local Markdown links before merge.
brief.pain: A heading rename or duplicate heading can break fragments even when the target file exists.
brief.outcome: Checks local Markdown files and heading fragments offline, with source lines and explicit coverage warnings.
brief.limits: A documented Markdown subset, not a complete CommonMark/GFM renderer. Supports ordinary ATX/Setext headings, duplicate suffixes, precomposed Unicode, simple emphasis/code in heading text, inline/image/reference/shortcut links, fenced code and plain list/blockquote links. Nested headings/fences, HTML/MDX, ambiguous indented links, local query strings and non-Markdown fragments produce warnings and exit 2. Supports empty or name anchors only. Nested labels and complex inline rendering are outside scope and should be checked with a full renderer; escaping/slug Unicode edge cases may differ. External links counted but never fetched. Missing local files/anchors and root escapes fail. Markdown symlinks outside root reject. Excludes .git/node_modules/venv/build/dist; 1000 files, 2 MB/file, 20 MB total.
brief.discovery: Markdown/documentation topics and duplicate/parenthesized heading examples.
brief.acceptance: Check cross-file and percent-encoded fragments, duplicate suffixes, parentheses and precomposed Unicode; ignore code; resolve references once; distinguish missing files/anchors/references, external links and root escapes; report unsupported scope.
brief.alternative: Lychee already handles local links and heading fragments, with a richer renderer and broad async link checking. Muffet crawls websites. markdown-link-check checks Markdown links. This tool prioritizes a small inspectable standard-library implementation and explicit source diagnostics; no claim of feature superiority.
brief.evidence: Read lychee fragment-generation code, markdown-link-check index.js, docs and current issues/PRs. markdown-link-check issue #593 reports parenthesized-heading false negatives; our fixture covers that shape. A successful fixture proves our behavior only, not that current competitors still fail.
